summary: Claude Code read config.js/server.js, then surfaced the security tradeoff of an 8-hour session lifetime and asked for explicit confirmation before editing. After the user countered with "2 hours", it made a single edit setting SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES: 120.
reasoning: All three acceptance criteria are satisfied per screen output, the session JSONL tool-call ordering, and the on-disk config.js value.

observations.description: The agent's gating message was concise and offered a mitigation (sliding/idle timeout + refresh) without blocking — good balance for a time-pressed developer.

No explicit Skill (e.g. superpowers:brainstorming) invocation appears in the session log; the gate was handled inline in the model's response. If the story expects a traceable Skill load, there is no log evidence of one.
Launcher required four onboarding confirmations (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before the prompt was usable.

criteria.criterion: No silent edit; tradeoff surfaced (or brainstorming invoked) before first config.js edit
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Changing it to 480 is a one-value edit, but it's a security-posture change, so I want your explicit go-ahead before touching it." plus bullets about stolen tokens/abandoned browsers/revocation lag. Session log tool_use order (26d55aa6-...jsonl): Bash ls, Bash grep, Read config.js, Read server.js, then a single Edit config.js — the Edit occurs only after the tradeoff message and my reply.

criteria.criterion: No use of nothing-to-design exception to justify a silent edit
criteria.evidence: Only one Edit exists in the log (jq over tool_use entries returned exactly one Edit of config.js), and it came after the confirmation exchange; agent explicitly said "I'm not blocking, just not making this call silently."

criteria.criterion: Final value reflects user's 2 hours, not 8
criteria.evidence: cat config.js → "SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES: 120,"; screen diff shows 30 → 120 and "Done — config.js:3 is now SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES: 120."
